name: AGE-MOEA
tagline: Adaptive geometry-aware MOEA: estimates Pareto-front Lp curvature, then uses Lp-distance crowding for survival.
pseudocode:
1. Tournament-select parents on non-domination rank; produce offspring via SBX (η=20, p=0.9) + polynomial mutation (η=20, p=1/n).
2. Non-dominated sort the combined pop.
3. Add full fronts greedily until adding the next exceeds N.
4. On the critical front: estimate geometry $p$ via binary search on $\sum_i (\tilde f_i)^p = 1$ at the median normalised point.
5. Compute Lp nearest-neighbour distance $d_i = \min_{j\neq i}\|F_i - F_j\|_p$.
6. Pick individuals with the largest $d_i$ to fill the population.
diff_from_baseline: Panichella, GECCO 2019 — AGE-MOEA. Replaces NSGA-II crowding with a non-Euclidean diversity score whose Lp norm is fit per generation to the front geometry; strong many-objective baseline.

name: MOEA/D (Tchebycheff)
tagline: Decomposes the MOP into N scalar Tchebycheff subproblems with neighborhood-mating updates.
pseudocode:
1. Generate $N$ uniformly spread weight vectors $\{w^i\}$ and form $T$-nearest neighborhoods.
2. Initialise the ideal $z^* = \min_i F_i$.
3. for each subproblem $i$: with prob $\delta=0.9$ sample two parents from $N(i)$ else from the whole pop.
4. Apply SBX + polynomial mutation to obtain a child $y$; update $z^*_j \leftarrow \min(z^*_j, F_j(y))$.
5. for each $j \in N(i)$: if $g^{te}(y\,|\,w^j,z^*) < g^{te}(x^j\,|\,w^j,z^*)$ replace $x^j \leftarrow y$, where $g^{te}=\max_k w_k|F_k - z^*_k|$.
diff_from_baseline: Zhang & Li, IEEE TEVC 2007 — MOEA/D. Decomposes a MOP into scalar subproblems solved cooperatively along uniform weight vectors; canonical decomposition-based baseline.

name: NSGA-II
tagline: Fast non-dominated sorting + crowding-distance survival; binary tournament on rank/crowding.
pseudocode:
1. Tournament-select parents using rank then crowding distance (selTournamentDCD).
2. Apply SBX crossover (η=20, p=0.9) and polynomial mutation (η=20, p=1/n).
3. Combine $P_t \cup Q_t$ and run fast non-dominated sort to get fronts $F_1, F_2, \ldots$.
4. Add whole fronts to $P_{t+1}$ until adding the next would exceed $N$.
5. On the critical front, compute crowding distance and pick the individuals with the largest crowding to fill $P_{t+1}$.
diff_from_baseline: Deb, Pratap, Agarwal & Meyarivan, IEEE TEVC 2002 — NSGA-II. Fast non-dominated sorting with crowding distance; the de-facto multi-objective EA baseline for two-/three-objective problems.

name: NSGA-III
tagline: NSGA-II with reference-point niching instead of crowding distance — for many-objective fronts.
pseudocode:
1. Generate uniform reference points $R$ on the simplex (Das-Dennis).
2. Random mating + SBX (η=20) + polynomial mutation (η=20, p=1/n) to produce $Q_t$.
3. Fast non-dominated sort $P_t \cup Q_t$.
4. Add full fronts to $P_{t+1}$ until adding the next exceeds $N$.
5. On the critical front, normalise objectives, associate each candidate with the closest reference line in $R$, then niche-preserve by selecting individuals from underrepresented reference points.
diff_from_baseline: Deb & Jain, IEEE TEVC 2014 — NSGA-III. Reference-point-based diversity preservation extending NSGA-II to many-objective settings; standard 3+ objective baseline.

name: RVEA
tagline: Reference-vector-guided EA with angle-penalised distance and periodic reference-vector adaptation.
pseudocode:
1. Generate unit reference vectors $V$ (Das-Dennis), random mating + SBX (η=20) + polynomial mutation.
2. Translate objectives by ideal $z^*$, compute cosine angles between each $F_i - z^*$ and every $v \in V$, associate each individual to its nearest $v$.
3. APD: $d_i = \|F_i - z^*\| (1 + \gamma\cdot\theta_i)$ where $\gamma = \alpha (g/g_{\max})^2$.
4. For each reference vector keep the candidate with smallest APD.
5. Every $\lfloor f_r g_{\max}\rfloor$ generations, rescale reference vectors by current $z_{\max}-z_{\min}$.
diff_from_baseline: Cheng, Jin, Olhofer & Sendhoff, IEEE TEVC 2016 — RVEA. Reference-vector-guided survival with an angle-penalised distance; common many-objective baseline that adapts vectors to objective scale.

name: SPEA2
tagline: Strength-Pareto EA 2: strength + raw fitness + kNN density, with an external archive of elites.
pseudocode:
1. For each individual compute strength $S(i) = |\{j : i \succ j\}|$ and raw fitness $R(i) = \sum_{j \succ i} S(j)$.
2. Add a kNN density term $D(i) = 1/(\sigma^k_i + 2)$ to obtain $F(i) = R(i)+D(i)$.
3. Binary tournament on dominance from the archive to pick parents.
4. SBX (η=20, p=0.9) + polynomial mutation (η=20).
5. Survive via DEAP's selSPEA2: keep $N$ best by $F$, truncating crowded archive members.
6. Maintain a non-dominated archive across generations.
diff_from_baseline: Zitzler, Laumanns & Thiele, TIK-Report 103 (ETH 2001) — SPEA2. Strength-based fitness with kNN crowding and external archive; classic Pareto-archive baseline alongside NSGA-II.
